resources.string: This mint charges %1$s to register an address, once. You can reserve the name now and pay when you like.
Pay %1$s to finish. The mint holds the name for a limited time; if the invoice runs out, you can try again.
This mint asks %1$s for an address, more than the %2$s this app accepts.
This mint can only give an address to the first account of a wallet. Choose another mint, or continue without an address.
Your funds are held by the mint you choose. Keep amounts small.
A name for this account on another mint, with the same recovery phrase. Payments to it arrive as notes on that mint, in this account. Your primary address stays where it is.
You can add a mint later. Until then, nothing can be received.
Bearer notes on Lightning. Ready in one tap.
The mint holds your money and makes the invoices you get paid with. Pick one; you can add more later.
Pick a mint. If your recovery phrase holds money there, it is found.
This app doesn\'t work with that mint. Pick another one.
That isn\'t a mint this app can use: %1$s
This wallet has this mint already. Adding it again looks for your money there again.
This mint speaks an older version of the protocol. It works, but only the first account of a wallet can have an address there.
Looking for what your recovery phrase holds on this mint, account by account.
This mint now shows another signing key than a moment ago, so it wasn\'t added. Check that it is the mint you meant.
The mint is added. Your new wallet uses it from now on.
The mint is added. Nothing of your recovery phrase was found on it.
You can receive with an invoice and get an address later in Settings.
Already taken. Try one of these:
Couldn\'t check right now. You can still try.
Payments to this address arrive in this wallet. Share it with anyone who wants to pay you.
Another name for this account on %1$s. Payments to any of its addresses arrive in the same balance.
Pick the name people will use to pay you on %1$s.

The words don\'t fit together. A word may be wrong or out of order.
Your balance comes back, and so does the address the app suggested when you set it up. Past activity and other addresses aren\'t part of the recovery phrase.
This recovery phrase is already in this wallet, as the account “%1$s”. For another address, add one on that account\'s page under Settings → Wallets.
It\'s registered, but the app can\'t double-check that payments reach this wallet. Try a small payment first.
The fee could not be paid. The name stays reserved.
The reservation ran out before the fee was paid. You can try again.
Couldn\'t reach it: %1$s. Check the address and your connection.
It stopped before it was done: %1$s. Try again; what was found stays.
Looks for everything your recovery phrase holds and adds what it finds. It only looks; nothing is moved.
The scan didn\'t get through everywhere. Try again; what was found stays.
The wallet is removed from this phone. Money of a restored wallet stays with its recovery phrase; you can restore it again any time.
A new account in this wallet: its own balance and addresses, the same recovery phrase. Nothing else to set up.
Checking what this account already holds. This can take a moment.
%1$s couldn\'t be reached to check what this account already holds, so it wasn\'t added. Try again in a moment.
People pay you at this address, on %1$s. If you had one there, type it to take it back.
